d: The most common functional ovarian cyst: a follicle that fails to rupture and keeps filling with fluid, forming a thin-walled simple cyst that usually resolves within one or two cycles.
Metastatic carcinoma in both ovaries made of mucin-filled signet-ring cells, usually from a gastric primary; the ovaries are enlarged, solid and often bilateral.
An ovarian epithelial tumor with stratification and atypia but no destructive stromal invasion; its peritoneal implants are usually noninvasive and most patients are cured by surgery.
A TP53-mutant carcinoma confined to the epithelium of the fimbriated fallopian tube; it is the precursor of most high-grade serous carcinomas and is often found in BRCA carriers' tubes.
Glomerulus-like structures of a central blood vessel wrapped by tumor cells in a space lined by tumor cells; they are the histologic hallmark of yolk sac tumor, which secretes AFP.
Small follicle-like rosettes of granulosa cells around eosinophilic material; with grooved coffee-bean nuclei, they identify the estrogen-making granulosa cell tumor.
